title: Isolation of Microbiota-Derived Membrane Vesicles from Mouse Blood and Colon
author: Erttmann, Gekara
materials: Millex 13 mm PVDF .22 μm Sterile RUO
Millex 13 mm PVDF .45 μm Sterile RUO
test tube shakers Genie Vortex Mixer
sterile 1.5 mL low protein binding collection tube

steps.title: Harvest colon luminal content
steps.instruction: Euthanize 8 mice (16 for two samples) by cervical dislocation, disinfect the ventral surface with 70 % ethanol, make a ventral incision from sternum to anus, remove the skin, open the peritoneal cavity without damaging internal organs, set aside stomach and small intestine, cut below the cecum, isolate the proximal colon and cut the rectum, place the colon in a sterile Petri dish, gently press to expel luminal material into the colon lumen, collect the luminal content with a sterile Merck Corning single‑use spatula (flat end, #CLS3007) into a 50 mL reaction tube containing 10 mL ice‑cold DPBS, and keep the tube on ice.

steps.title: Pre‑clear colon supernatant
steps.instruction: Vortex the colon content tube for 30 s at ~1500 rpm (Genie Vortex Mixer, speed 6). Centrifuge at 4,000 ×g, 4 °C for 5 min; transfer supernatant to a new 15 mL tube. Centrifuge the transferred supernatant at 4,000 ×g, 4 °C for 10 min, transfer to a new tube; repeat this 10‑min spin once more. Finally, spin the supernatant at 6,000 ×g, 4 °C for 10 min and transfer to a new tube. Filter sequentially through a 0.45 µm syringe filter then a 0.2 µm syringe filter into a fresh 15 mL tube (final volume ≈4 mL). Keep the filtered fluid on ice while preparing the chromatography columns.

steps.title: Equilibrate size‑exclusion columns
steps.instruction: Allow qEVoriginal / 70 nm Gen 2 columns and sterile‑filtered DPBS to reach 20 °C (operational range 18‑24 °C). Assemble the IZON column stand, insert the columns into the stand, and place 15 mL reaction tubes beneath each column. Equilibrate each column with at least 40 mL sterile‑filtered DPBS by repeatedly adding 2 mL DPBS to the top‑filter, collecting the flow‑through in the tube below, and continuing until ≥40 mL has passed; never let the top‑filter run dry. After equilibration, replace the luer slip cap to seal the column bottom and close the upper cap if the column is not used immediately.

steps.title: Load sample and collect fractions
steps.instruction: Open the column’s upper cap, remove residual buffer above the top‑filter while keeping the luer slip cap in place, then load 500 µL of the concentrated serum or colon fluid onto the centre of the filter. Immediately remove the luer slip cap and collect eluate in 0.5 mL fractions using 1.5 mL low‑protein‑binding tubes. After the sample has entered, add up to 2 mL DPBS to the top‑filter to level it without diluting the sample. Discard fractions 1‑6 (void volume) or combine them into two tubes for convenience. Collect fractions 7‑9 (MV‑rich) separately and store at 4 °C. Optionally collect fractions 10‑12 (protein‑rich) for downstream analysis. After fraction collection, wash the column with 20‑30 mL DPBS, keep the top‑filter covered with DPBS, and store the column at 4 °C. Columns may be reused up to five times provided the flow rate remains unchanged.

steps.title: Optional vesicle and protein quantification
steps.instruction: Measure vesicle concentration in each collected fraction with an Izon qNano system and determine protein concentration using the Pierce BCA protein assay kit.
